$comment: Text/background pairs that must keep meeting WCAG 2.2 contrast, checked in both themes.
The site measures AAA on almost every pair today. Nothing was holding it there: the palette is
themed, green is opt-in and had never been measured at all, and a token nudged for aesthetic
reasons moves every pair built on it at once. Contrast is the accessibility property most easily
lost by a change that looks like an improvement.
WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (>=24px, or >=18.66px bold) and for
non-text UI. AAA is 7:1 and 4.5:1. The bar here is AA - AAA is recorded where it is met so a drop
to merely-AA is visible in a diff rather than silent.
SCOPE, stated plainly. This checks declared palette pairs, not every rendered element. It cannot
see gradient-filled text or a label sitting on a gradient button, because those are painted by
background-image and have no computed colour to read. Those were measured in a browser against
the darkest stop of each gradient - hero headline 7.56, section eyebrow 11.79, primary CTA label
7.23 - and the darkest stop is recorded here as a literal so a palette change still moves it.
A full render-time sweep is P2-14 and needs a browser in CI.

pairs.note: The tightest pair on the site at 4.62, and used at 9px for micro-labels. Any darkening of px-faint or lightening of px-bg fails here first, which is why it is listed.
Links and step numerals. Themed - checked in blue and green.
The darkest companion hue, and the most likely to fail.
Alpha marker and the stale-data badge.
Dark label on the primary button. The button is a gradient; px-accent-400 is its darkest stop, so this is the worst case a reader sees.
70px gradient headline, large-text threshold. Same darkest stop as the accent pair; listed separately so the requirement is explicit rather than inferred.
